newsitem.title: ITALY: Antarctic trekker on verge of success.
newsitem.headline: Antarctic trekker on verge of success.

text.p: Norwegian explorer Borge Ousland was on the verge of completing an unsupported crossing of Antarctica on Wednesday, two months after setting out on his solo trek across the ice, his sponsors said.
Ousland set out on November 15 from Berkner Island in the Weddel Sea to try to cross Antarctica to the Scott Base on Ross Island.

A statement from the sponsors said Ousland, who is using skis, a sled and a giant "para-wing" sail to help speed his journey, was a little less than 100 km (63 miles) from the finish at 1130 GMT on Wednesday.
His aim is to become the first man to complete the crossing of more than 2,800 km (1,750 miles) without the help of dogs or motorised support.
Ousland reached the halfway mark of his journey, the South Pole, on December 19.
He had also reached the South Pole during a first attempt over the route in 1995 but frostbite forced him to give up after 44 days on the world's coldest continent.
In his earlier attempt Ousland was racing explorer Roger Mear to set a new endurance record, but the Briton also had to abandon his walk after vital equipment failed.
